# The hottest each thermoblock's casting gets while the controller holds its heater

**Generated by `firmware/emulation/tools/run_casting_peak.py`. Do not edit by hand — re-run `python3 firmware/emulation/tools/run_casting_peak.py`.**

> **Diagnostic, not a board input.** These peaks are those of the control as it shipped. This record is not an input to any board until the regeneration criterion of DEL-CASTING-MARGIN-HELD-IN-EVERY-PHASE has run and the record has been regenerated from the corrected control. The steam peak is bounded by the course's draw length: it is the peak of a draw of that length, and the draw-length table below shows how it moves with a longer one.

The proof-of-life removal interval starts from the temperature a heater's casting has when the controller stops, and the commanded figure does not bound it: the coffee loop controls the water leaving the block and the steam loop controls pressure during a draw, and in both the casting runs hotter than the commanded figure by an amount no declared figure fixes. This record is the hottest the plant model's casting reaches while the shipped control path is holding the heater, taken over every operating phase the controller commands and every corner of the declared error whose machine the control path accepts; the corners it refuses are listed under the corners below.

Each heater is run on its own, since the two heated masses are independent, with the machine built from one corner's coefficients and the control path held at the description that shipped. The corners are the control path's own enumeration, read back through the same reading the protection-margin record uses: each end of each coefficient carrying a declared error, on its own, plus each stated joint corner. The corners combine by the worst single corner and never by summing or in quadrature. The machine at the declared coefficients is run as well and reported beside them.

Each loop's declared sensing error is added to the hottest casting temperature the runs report, as a simultaneous degradation. The controller is run on the plant's true values, so a sensor reading low, which holds the casting hotter than the control path believes, is not otherwise in the peak.

Nothing here is a measurement. The casting is the model's, graded **inferred**, and measuring it on the machine is not what this record does.

The supply this was run against is the declared 216–253 V span about the 230 V nominal, as the description's accounts state it. How each element rating's declared error was derived from that supply is set out in the description's account beside the rating; this record does not check that derivation.

A replacement model is read by naming it: `--description`, `--limits`, `--tolerance` and `--steam-declaration` each point the same method at another file.

Targets, each the highest the control path admits and read rather than chosen:

| Served | Target (C) | Where it is read from |
|---|---|---|
| coffee | 100.0 | the highest target the protection-margin reading narrows the loop's admission to (bound: over-saturation) |
| hot water | 96.0 | the number just under the 96.0 C drinking-temperature ceiling `firmware/params/tolerance.declaration` declares, which the control path refuses a drinking-point target at or above |
| steam | 186.1 | the highest ready temperature the steam loop comes up at, as the protection-margin reading reports it (the declared ready temperature is 137.0 C); at a corner whose own machine admits less, that lower one, because the steam draw builds the loop from the description of the machine it is run against |

Each coffee-thermoblock course warms the machine from cold and holds it with no draw (40000 control intervals of 10 ms, lengthened if the casting has not come to rest), then for each of two pump levels, 300 permille of full pump scale (the level the sweep draws a shot at) and 1000 permille (full pump scale), runs a delivery of 6000 intervals, a recovery of 40000, a delivery followed on the next interval by a second of 6000, and a recovery of 40000. Each steam course does the same with the wand opened at 1.0 millilitres a second for 2000 intervals and recoveries of 40000. A recovery that has not passed its maximum and settled back to within 0.25 C of the holding value for 1000 intervals by its end is lengthened and run again, up to 4 times its length, and refused beyond that.

## The peak under control

The figure for each thermoblock is the hottest casting temperature any run reported, over every control interval, at the worst single corner, plus that loop's declared sensing error. Grade: **inferred** from the plant model.

| Thermoblock | Peak casting temperature (C) | Declared sensing error (C) | Peak plus sensing error (C) | Phase | Corner | Served | Coefficient | End |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coffee thermoblock | 156.8 | 2.0 | 158.8 | warm-up | 2 | coffee | brew.thermal_mass_j_per_k | low |
| Steam thermoblock | 194.3 | 2.0 | 196.3 | delivery | 48 | steam | steam.feed_flow_ml_per_s | low |

The coffee thermoblock's peak is reached in its warm-up phase, at interval 3310 of a course of 236000, at corner 2 (brew.thermal_mass_j_per_k, low end), commanded at 100.0 C.
The steam thermoblock's peak is reached in its delivery phase, at interval 83550 of a course of 126000, at corner 48 (steam.feed_flow_ml_per_s, low end), commanded at 186.1 C.

## What each corner reached

Every corner run, with the hottest casting it reached in any phase. A corner at the end `params/thermoblock.md` calls one-sided is run too and carries `not-claimed`: the description stands behind no machine there, and the peak is included all the same because it can only raise a safety figure. Every corner the enumeration covers is run, except a steam corner whose machine the control path itself refuses to come up against, which is listed below with the reason and left out of the worst; the tool refuses to write this record when a corner produces no machine at all.

**2 of the 51 steam corners were not run, because the control path refuses the machine they build.** The control path fails closed on a believed description from which it cannot establish its protection margin at every declared corner, and each of these corners, once the description's own declared error is applied at every declared corner on top of it, leaves such a description. ## How the steam peak depends on how long the wand is held open

The steam courses above hold the wand open for 20 seconds, about what a jug of milk takes. A draw has no end of its own, so the steam figure above is the figure for a draw of that length and for no longer one. At the declared coefficients a draw held longer does not climb higher than the longest of the lengths below (186.1 C against 186.1 C at 20 seconds). The corners are not run at the longer draws, so that is no statement about them. The hottest casting temperature over the draw, at the machine's declared coefficients with the ready temperature at 186.1 C, by how long the wand is held:

| Wand held open (s) | Peak casting temperature (C) |
|---|---|
| 20 | 186.1 |
| 60 | 186.1 |
| 120 | 186.1 |
| 300 | 186.1 |

## What this does not settle

Whether the casting is where the model says it is. No casting on this machine has been instrumented, the declared errors the corners are taken from are judgements rather than readings, and the thermal masses and loss coefficients that set how far the casting runs ahead of the water leaving it are estimates.

How long a steam draw lasts. The steam figure is for the draw the courses above open the wand for. The table above shows what a longer one does in the model, and nothing in this record says how long a draw the controller may be asked to hold.

The trip points. This record stops at the hottest casting; the time a heater takes to climb from it to its protection's trip point is not derived here or in the controller boards' figures record, which only quotes this record's figures and keeps the interval pending. It is derived from this record's peak by SOL-PROOF-OF-LIFE-INTERVAL-DERIVED-FROM-HELD-CASTING-PEAK, once the control holds the casting below its trip point.
